lead.zh-Hans: 铁塔很好认，碰面的说法还要再商量。
lead.en: The tower was easy to find. Our meeting point needed work.

text.zh-Hans: 到了巴黎，我和一位旅人约好看埃菲尔铁塔。它为1889年的世界博览会而建，我在远处已经认出了它，便觉得“塔那边见”说得很清楚。走近才发现，我们各自站在了不同的地方。我把便签翻过来，补上碰头的小位置。铁塔负责醒目，便签负责具体。
text.en: A fellow traveler and I planned to see the Eiffel Tower, built for the 1889 World's Fair. I spotted it from afar and thought “near the tower” was excellent meeting guidance. We still found different places to stand. My note acquired a more exact meeting spot. The tower supplied the landmark; the note handled the details.
Agree on a clearer meeting description
Notice how the tower stands out

lead.zh-Hans: 一块玻璃，让我多看见了一层庭院。
lead.en: The courtyard acquired another layer in the glass.

text.zh-Hans: 在卢浮宫的拿破仑庭院，我停下来望着贝聿铭设计的玻璃金字塔。玻璃后面和玻璃上的影子叠在一起，我一会儿追着边线看，一会儿又看回周围的建筑。便签上只留了一个三角和一个小方框，提醒自己：刚才那一眼，别急着选只看哪一层。
text.en: In the Louvre's Cour Napoléon, I paused by I. M. Pei's glass Pyramid. What lay beyond the glass mingled with reflections on its surface. I followed an edge, then looked back at the surrounding buildings. A triangle and a small square on my note will remind me to let both views stay for a moment.
Tell someone which layer caught your eye
Follow another edge across the glass

lead.zh-Hans: 今天的小菜单，先记下了一声轻响。
lead.en: Today's little menu began with a sound.

text.zh-Hans: 我在巴黎买了一份法棍面包。掰开时，外壳轻轻响了一下，里面露出软软的、带着气孔的面包心。我低头看了一会儿，才想起手上这份是午饭，不是要交的观察作业。小菜单上画了断面，旁边写“一声轻响，然后开吃”。这回标点也很香。
text.en: I bought some baguette in Paris. The crust made a little crack as I broke it, revealing soft bread and uneven pockets inside. I studied it until I remembered lunch was waiting in my hands. The menu sketch has a cross-section and one instruction: “A small crunch, then eat.” An unusually fragrant piece of punctuation.
Describe the little sound to someone
Notice the pockets inside the bread

lead.zh-Hans: 圆圆的甜点没有起点，第一口有。
lead.en: The pastry had no beginning. My first bite did.

text.zh-Hans: 下午，我尝了一份巴黎布雷斯特泡芙。环形泡芙夹着果仁糖奶油，我拿着小叉子，先在圆圈边上犹豫了一小下。从哪儿吃都可以，偏偏想给这一口选个开头。吃完后，我在小菜单上画了个短箭头，写“从这里”。那是我下午的起点，不是甜点的规定。
text.en: In the afternoon I tried a Paris-Brest, a ring of choux pastry with praline cream. My fork hovered while I chose a beginning on a shape that had none. Afterwards, a short arrow on my menu marked the first bite: “Start here.” It records my afternoon, not a rule for pastry.
Name the afternoon's first bite
Find where the little arrow begins

lead.zh-Hans: 两张菜单，刚好轮流当了一回提示卡。
lead.en: Two menus took turns being cue cards.

text.zh-Hans: 吃过法棍和巴黎布雷斯特泡芙，我把两张菜单带到歇脚的桌上。一位旅人想听我讲今天吃了什么，我先把菜名慢慢念了一遍，讲到一半，自己又指错了纸。我们把两张换回去，决定一人拿一张提示。这回故事总算没有让面包冒充甜点了。
text.en: After baguette and a Paris-Brest, I showed my two menus to a fellow traveler. I read the names slowly before describing the day, then promptly pointed to the wrong sheet. We put them back and each held a cue card. The bread no longer had to play the pastry in my account of Paris.
Take turns introducing the menus
Match each name with its sketch

lead.zh-Hans: 一份从掰开开始，一份从选一边开始。
lead.en: One began with a break; the other, a choice of edge.

text.zh-Hans: 晚上整理巴黎的小菜单，法棍那张让我想起掰开外壳的一声轻响，巴黎布雷斯特那张则留着第一口的箭头。食物都吃好了，两个开头还在纸上。我把它们放在同一页，没有再加结尾。明天翻到这里，说不定会先想起那支犹豫的小叉子。
text.en: Sorting my Paris menus that evening, the baguette sketch brought back its small crack of crust; the Paris-Brest kept its first-bite arrow. Both foods were long eaten, but their beginnings remained. I placed the menus together without adding an ending. Tomorrow I may remember the hesitant little fork first.

text.zh-Hans: 说说哪一个开头更清楚
text.en: Share which beginning feels clearer
Look at the two beginnings together

lead.zh-Hans: 你说“{reply}”，我们重新写了碰面的便签。
lead.en: We took your suggestion, “{reply}”, back to our meeting note.

text.zh-Hans: 我和旅人把“塔那边见”换成了两行：先写我们一起认得的位置，再写到了就挥一下手。为了别把挥手也忘掉，我在下面添了一个背邮包的小身影。两行字折在卡里，展开就是我们的碰面办法。下回再见，铁塔不用替我们猜谁站在哪儿了。
text.en: The traveler and I replaced “near the tower” with two lines: a spot we both recognized, then a wave on arrival. I added a tiny figure with a mailbag so the waving would not be forgotten too. Folded together, the lines make our own meeting card. Next time the Eiffel Tower can leave the introductions to us.
Leave the little waving figure a message
Unfold the card and read the two lines

lead.zh-Hans: 巴黎的问候，掰开以后软软的。
lead.en: A greeting from Paris, soft in the middle.

text.zh-Hans: 法棍一掰开，酥脆的外壳就落了些碎屑。我把纸袋往前移，接住掉下来的小块，里头柔软的面包露出大小不一的气孔。又回巴黎，原本只想买点熟悉的食物，吃着吃着，倒为一个没抹平的孔看了好久。邻座以为我在发愁，我把面包举给他看。我们都笑了，纸袋里的碎屑还得慢慢吃完。
text.en: The baguette crackled as I broke it, sending crumbs toward my paper bag. Inside, the soft bread was full of uneven pockets. A familiar loaf had seemed an easy choice for my return to Paris. Then I spent so long examining a hole that my neighbour thought something was wrong. I held up the bread to explain. We both laughed. I still had the crumbs in the bag to finish.
Talk about the pockets in the bread

text.zh-Hans: 看看外壳和里面的不同
text.en: Compare the crust and the inside
